data.title: ROI-Anthropic's super-sized debut, Nvidia China crisis and a GTA heist: The financial week in five charts
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Every Friday, Reuters Open Interest (ROI) distills the financial week into five key charts, spotlighting the major trends, surprises and overlooked moves that defined the past five days.

1.SIZE MATTERS

MIKE DOLAN, ROI Finance & Markets Columnist: Anthropic's blockbuster IPO this week crowned a bumper year for US new listings in dollar terms, lifting 2026 IPO proceeds above the 2021 peak.

But as the year ​winds down, the actual number of IPOs in 2026 remains below last year's total and well below the average of the past decade. So while there is still a lot of capital available for new listings, the bar for making the cut has been raised. What this means for the future performance of the latest crop of mega caps remains to be seen.

2. CHIPPED ARMOR

JAMIE MCGEEVER, ROI Markets Columnist: The Nvidia ( NVDA ) scandal has thrust a blinding spotlight on the US-China "AI arms race." Washington is tightening curbs on Chinese firms accessing advanced US chips, which Beijing still needs to keep its AI engine going.

For its part, Nvidia ( NVDA ) says it is effectively shut out of the Chinese market, although a Reuters review found more than $3 billion in Chinese computing projects used its restricted chips. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) share price is taking a hit, a beating that actually started well before CEO Jensen Huang resigned, shedding roughly $2 trillion of market cap in around six weeks.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stellar earnings report on Tuesday did little to stem the bleeding, especially given reports that the company is now the subject of a US Securities and Exchange Commission probe.

3. TAPS WIDE OPEN

RON BOUSSO, ROI Energy Columnist: Global benchmark Brent crude prices have fallen more than 20% since the start of the month, settling into a no-war, no-peace range just above $90 a barrel.

Gulf oil production and exports have risen steadily since August, easing pressure on global supplies, even as Middle East tensions have escalated, with multiple Iranian strikes on tankers in recent weeks. The poster child for this shaky new normal is Saudi Arabia. Its October oil output rose above its 2025 average despite continued attacks from Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi militia on Saudi energy infrastructure.

4. GAME ON

ANNA SZYMANSKI, ROI Editor-in-Charge: Grand Theft Auto VI arrived on Thursday after a 13-year wait and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, making it one of the most anticipated video-game releases in history. It is expected to generate billions of dollars in first-week sales, delivering a major boost to the industry.

Its impact may extend beyond retail. Fans booked time off for marathon sessions, turning launch day into an unofficial holiday. Whether this leads to missed deadlines and angry bosses or simply a temporary, much-needed respite for stressed workers remains to be seen.

5. SHENZHEN REALITY CHECK

JAMIE MCGEEVER, ROI Markets Columnist: US President Donald Trump has no shortage of economic troubles - inflation, rising interest rates and the Nvidia ( NVDA ) scandal, to name a few. But when he met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen this week, Xi may well have looked at Trump's hand with envy. China's domestic economy is still struggling with the fallout from the country's real estate bust, business investment is plummeting, and the stock market is down 20% since the summer. The only real bright spot is exports, boosted by tech and AI. But what if the AI bubble deflates?

data.title: AI Concerns, Oil Outlook Undercut European Bourses Midday
data.description:
06:52 AM EST, 11/20/2026 (MT Newswires) -- European bourses tracked lower midday Friday as traders joined the global risk-off mood on tech stocks, while oil shares fell back on oversupply concerns.

The pan-continental Stoxx Europe 600 Index was off 1.1% mid-session.

Food stocks led gains on continental trading floors, while oil shares joined AI- and semiconductor-related stocks on the downside.

Brent crude-oil futures were down 2% at $90.18 a barrel, in midday trades.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) projected a global oil supply would exceed demand in Q4, with an expanding surplus 2027, in its World Energy Outlook released Thursday.

Investors also eyed Wall Street futures in the red, and lower closes overnight on Asian exchanges.

In economic news, producer prices in Germany rose by 8.1% on year in October, and by 1.4% from September, Destatis reported. Higher energy bills were cited.

In the sectors, the Stoxx Europe 600 Technology Index was down 3.4%, and the Stoxx 600 Banks Index lost 1.7% in mid-session action.

The Stoxx Europe 600 Oil and Gas Index eased 1.8%, while the Stoxx 600 Europe Food and Beverage Index bucked trends to incline 1.1%.

The REITE, a European REIT index, fell 0.2%.

On the national market indexes, Germany's DAX was down 1.6%, and the FTSE 100 in London lost 0.6%. The CAC 40 in Paris was down 1.2%, and Spain's IBEX 35 eased 1%.

Yields on benchmark 10-year German bonds were lower, near 3.32%.

The Euro Stoxx 50 volatility index was up 18.5% at 26.70, indicating above-average volatility for European stock markets in the next 30 days, a negative signal. A reading above 20 indicates choppier markets ahead, while below 20 suggests calmer exchanges.

data.title: France's EDF nears investment decision on new nuclear reactors, say sources
data.description:
* Utility targets December investment decision for six nuclear reactors

* Investment decision expected even without EU state aid approval

* EDF expected to auction of about 3,000 MW of electricity to reduce dominant market position

By Forrest Crellin

PARIS, Nov 20 (Reuters) - France's EDF plans to start hiring staff, placing orders and awarding contracts next year for six new nuclear reactors, even before securing final EU approval for a state-backed financing package, two sources familiar with the plans said.

The state-owned utility is pressing ahead with Europe's largest nuclear expansion project in decades, seeking to avoid the lengthy delays and ballooning costs that have plagued its past projects in France and Britain.

The programme to replace France's ageing reactors aims to bring a first reactor online by 2038 and is expected to cost more than €70 billion ($76.85 billion) for all six, with the government financing 60% through a zero-interest loan.

Under EU rules for state aid, the loan requires approval by the European Commission. But negotiations between Brussels and Paris are dragging on as the authority seeks assurance that the project will not give EDF greater market dominance.

EDF will in the meantime, however, take a provisional investment decision, the two people briefed on the plans said. That will allow it to begin ordering parts, hiring staff, awarding contracts and preparing construction sites to ensure the project sticks to its timeline.

"EDF wants to start fabricating the parts. People are already in place and ready to do that. We don't want to wait for that for one or two years," one of the people said.

French newspaper Les Echos reported earlier this week that EDF is discussing contracts worth €14 billion with builders Bouygues, Eiffage and Vinci.

EDF declined to comment on the contracts. It did not immediately respond to questions about the investment decision.

INVESTMENT DECISION SET FOR LATE DECEMBER

The nuclear expansion plan was developed at the outset of Russia's war in Ukraine, which caused a European energy crunch and coincided with an unexpected maintenance period that took half of France's reactors offline for checks and repairs.

It is intended to replace output from reactors approaching the end of their operating lives and help prevent a sharp decline in French nuclear generation from the middle of the century.

EDF's board is expected to review the investment decision in mid-December, finalise the terms during the third week of the month and take the provisional decision before year-end, the people said.

The European Commission's decision on the loan may not be made until well into next year, but EDF is optimistic an agreement will be reached with Brussels, the first source said.

The Commission did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

EDF is under pressure to launch the project before next year's presidential election, which could slow government decision-making and reshape French energy policy.

Marine Le Pen's far-right party, currently the frontrunner in polls, supports nuclear energy. However, Jean-Luc Melenchon, seen in polls reaching a second round but a long shot to win, is anti-nuclear.

To secure EU approval for the financing package, EDF has proposed auctioning 3,000 megawatts of output through long-term contracts to rival suppliers, ensuring competitors also benefit from the state-backed loan, the sources said.

The volume, equivalent to about 7% of EDF's annual output, would give competitors access to some of the electricity generated by the new plants rather than allowing EDF to reserve all of the output for its own customers or bilateral contracts.

($1 = 0.9108 euros)

(Reporting by Forrest Crellin; Editing by Dominique Patton and Joe Bavier)

data.title: American Resources Corporation and ReElement Technologies Selected as Part of Winning U.S.-Led Consortium for Kenya's Strategic Mrima Hill Critical Minerals Project
data.description:
FISHERS, IN / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / American Resources Corporation ( AREC ) ("American Resources") and ReElement Technologies Corporation ("ReElement"), a leading U.S. operator of advanced critical mineral refining and separation technologies in which American Resources ( AREC ) maintains a strategic minority ownership interest, today announced that the Frontier Minerals Consortium ("Frontier"), of which both companies are members, has been selected by the Government of Kenya as the successful bidder in the competitive international tender for the Mrima Hill Niobium, Rare Earth Elements and Other Minerals Development Project in Kwale County, Kenya.

The selection, announced by Kenya's Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs, represents a significant milestone in advancing one of the world's most strategically important undeveloped rare earth and niobium deposits. Frontier has been selected to enter exclusive negotiations toward a prospecting license, with subsequent activities subject to applicable regulatory approvals, community engagement and licensing requirements.

Frontier is partnered with American Resources ( AREC ), ReElement and Bunker Hill Silver Corp. ("Bunker Hill"), bringing together complementary expertise in mineral resource development, critical minerals supply chains and advanced refining technologies. The consortium's integrated approach is designed to support the development of a comprehensive mine-to-material value chain, emphasizing domestic processing and refining, local economic participation and long-term value creation in Kenya.

Through its Platform Orchestration model, American Resources ( AREC ) serves as a strategic supply-chain and commercial development partner, connecting mineral resource opportunities with advanced processing and refining capabilities, including those of ReElement, and downstream markets.

As part of its participation in the consortium, American Resources ( AREC ) expects to hold an equity interest in Frontier, subject to definitive agreements among the consortium partners. ReElement participates as the consortium's advanced refining technology partner, contributing its proprietary chromatography-based separation and purification capabilities, with the opportunity to generate refining-related revenues through future technology deployment, processing and commercial arrangements, subject to feasibility studies and definitive agreements.

The consortium is pursuing a capital-efficient development strategy that includes potential non-dilutive financing, government-supported funding and other strategic financing alternatives. Consistent with its Platform Orchestration model, American Resources ( AREC ) expects to hold an equity interest in Frontier while minimizing direct capital requirements and actively supporting the consortium through feasibility and development. This approach is designed to create long-term economic value for American Resources ( AREC ) and its shareholders while advancing Kenya's critical mineral development and in-country value-chain objectives, subject to definitive agreements.

A Differentiated Mine-to-Material Development Strategy

A central component of Frontier's proposal is the development of an integrated critical minerals value chain within Kenya, extending beyond traditional resource extraction and concentrate exports to include domestic mineral processing, advanced separation and refining, workforce development and downstream market integration.

The consortium's selection reflects a proposal designed to address Kenya's stated objectives for domestic mineral beneficiation, local economic participation, environmental stewardship and responsible resource development.

American Resources ( AREC ) contributes its international resource sourcing, feedstock aggregation, strategic partnerships and critical minerals supply-chain development capabilities. ReElement contributes its proprietary, patented chromatography-based separation and refining platform, designed to produce high-purity, specification-grade rare earth elements and other critical minerals through modular, scalable processing systems. Bunker Hill contributes mining, engineering, metallurgical processing and project development expertise, providing an integrated approach to evaluating and potentially developing the Mrima Hill resource.

Together, these capabilities are intended to support the development of a commercially sustainable supply chain that retains more economic value in Kenya while expanding access to strategically important critical minerals for U.S. and allied manufacturers.

Advanced U.S. Refining Technology Supporting Kenyan Value Creation

ReElement's chromatography-based technology represents a differentiated approach to critical mineral refining, utilizing water-based separation processes designed to reduce chemical consumption, energy requirements and environmental impacts compared with conventional solvent extraction methods.

Originally developed at Purdue University and licensed in 2021, the technology has since been advanced and commercialized through ReElement's proprietary research, engineering and intellectual property development. ReElement has validated separation and purification capabilities across 15 rare earth elements and additional critical minerals, achieving purities of up to 99.999% for select products.

The company commissioned its first commercial-scale chromatography columns for germanium production at the facility in August 2026 and continues to progressively scale its domestic refining capabilities.

ReElement's proposed role in the Mrima Hill project will focus on developing optimized commercial processing and refining flowsheets utilizing its proprietary chromatography-based technology. This approach is designed to support the phased deployment of modular refining infrastructure in Kenya, enabling the production of high-purity, value-added critical mineral products within the country, subject to project-specific technical, commercial and regulatory requirements. Beyond Mrima Hill, ReElement's participation is expected to create opportunities to evaluate additional critical mineral feedstocks throughout Kenya and the broader region, with the objective of leveraging potential shared refining infrastructure, enhancing capital efficiency and technology utilization, and supporting Kenya's emergence as a regional hub for advanced critical mineral refining.

This approach is intended to support the production of higher-value refined materials within Kenya rather than limiting the country's participation to the export of raw minerals or intermediate concentrates.

A Strategic Opportunity for Kenya and the United States

Mrima Hill contains historically identified rare earth and niobium mineralization, including elements important to permanent magnets, aerospace, advanced electronics and other strategic industries. Historical mineral resource estimates indicate significant mineralization; however, these estimates have not been verified as current mineral resources and will require further technical evaluation.

The project represents an opportunity to align Kenya's economic development and industrialization objectives with the United States' strategic interest in building diversified, secure, transparent and traceable critical mineral supply chains.

By supporting domestic processing and refining, the consortium's proposed development model seeks to create opportunities for Kenyan workers, technical professionals, suppliers and local communities while establishing additional sources of high-value critical materials for international manufacturers.

Mark C. Jensen, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of American Resources Corporation ( AREC ), commented: "This selection represents much more than an important milestone for the Frontier Minerals Consortium. It reflects a shared vision of how critical mineral resources can be developed to create lasting economic value for resource-rich countries while strengthening the industrial and national security interests of the United States and its allies.

"For too long, many resource-rich nations have participated primarily at the extraction stage of the global minerals supply chain, while much of the downstream processing, refining and economic value has been captured elsewhere. We believe the opportunity at Mrima Hill is to help change that model by bringing together world-class mining capabilities, advanced American refining technology and integrated supply-chain development.

"Our Platform Orchestration model is designed to create meaningful economic participation in strategic resource opportunities through partnerships and equity interests, while leveraging third-party capital and minimizing direct development expenditures. We believe this approach allows American Resources ( AREC ) to participate in globally significant projects while remaining focused on capital efficiency and the creation of long-term shareholder value.

"Importantly, this announcement is not the culmination of our efforts, but the beginning of a much broader opportunity. We look forward to working alongside the Government of Kenya, local communities and our consortium partners to advance a responsible, commercially sustainable development strategy that creates meaningful value for Kenya and strengthens critical mineral supply chains for the United States. We believe this collaborative approach can serve as a model for mutually beneficial partnerships in other resource-rich jurisdictions where we are actively developing relationships and opportunities."

Next Steps

Following the Government of Kenya's selection, Frontier intends to advance the required community engagement, regulatory and prospecting-license application processes in accordance with Kenyan law.

Subject to receipt of the necessary approvals, the consortium's proposed development program includes confirmation drilling, updated mineral resource evaluation, metallurgical test work, refining technology assessments, environmental and social studies, and preparation of a bankable feasibility study.

The feasibility process will focus on developing integrated mining, mineral processing and advanced refining flowsheets, leveraging ReElement's proprietary chromatography-based platform to support the production of high-purity, value-added critical minerals within Kenya. This approach is designed to establish a commercially viable, mine-to-material development model that maximizes in-country value-chain capture while supporting diversified critical mineral supply chains for the United States and its allies.

The consortium recognizes the environmental, cultural and social significance of Mrima Hill and intends to work with Kenyan authorities, local communities and other stakeholders to evaluate the project responsibly and in accordance with applicable requirements.

About American Resources Corporation ( AREC )

American Resources Corporation ( AREC ) operates a diversified critical materials platform through its Platform Orchestration strategy, which coordinates complementary capabilities across commercial feedstock origination, resource sourcing, industrial processing and advanced refining partnerships. This capital-efficient approach enables the Company to align resources, technologies and commercial relationships to evolving customer requirements and national priorities while strengthening U.S. and allied critical mineral supply chains.

The Company's operating platforms span conventional and unconventional resource sourcing, feedstock aggregation, recycling, processing and conditioning, complemented by its strategic ownership interest in ReElement Technologies Corporation, a leading U.S. advanced materials transformation and refining company. Through these complementary capabilities and strategic relationships, American Resources ( AREC ) seeks to connect diverse feedstock sources with advanced processing and refining solutions, enabling greater value chain capture and supporting growing commercial, industrial and defense-sector demand.

American Resources' ( AREC ) modular, asset-light business model emphasizes disciplined capital allocation, scalable operations and strategic partnerships. By coordinating specialized capabilities across the critical materials value chain without requiring traditional vertical integration, the Company seeks to expand commercial opportunities and support resilient, economically sustainable supply chains serving infrastructure, defense, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, energy and electrification markets.

For more information, visit americanresourcescorp.com or connect with the Company on Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn.

About ReElement Technologies Corporation

ReElement Technologies Corporation, a strategic portfolio holding of American Resources Corporation ( AREC ) , is a leading U.S. developer and operator of advanced materials transformation and refining technologies. Its modular, refining-first platform utilizes proprietary, patented chromatography-based separation and purification technology to transform diverse feedstocks - including primary mineral concentrates, recycled materials, industrial byproducts and other unconventional sources - into high-purity, specification-grade critical materials. ReElement's flexible technology enables the co-location of advanced refining capabilities closer to feedstock sources and downstream customers, supporting greater value chain capture while reducing chemical consumption and environmental impact. The Company supports secure, resilient U.S. and allied supply chains serving defense, aerospace, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, permanent magnets, energy and battery technologies.

For more information, visit reelementtech.com or connect with the Company on Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn.

Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of applicable securities laws, including statements regarding the Frontier Minerals Consortium's selection, the proposed Mrima Hill project, licensing and regulatory approvals, community engagement, mineral resource evaluation, feasibility studies, financing, future mining and refining activities, potential deployment of ReElement's technology, anticipated equity participation and commercial arrangements, anticipated economic benefits and the development of critical mineral supply chains.

These statements involve risks and uncertainties, including potential challenges to the tender outcome, the ability to obtain required licenses and community consents, environmental and cultural heritage considerations, technical and metallurgical performance, the verification of historical mineral resource estimates, financing availability, project economics, international regulatory developments and other risks described in American Resources' ( AREC ) filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. data.title: MORNING BID AMERICAS-AI's last stand?
data.description:
(The opinions expressed here are those of the author.)

By Anna Szymanski

LONDON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - From the Editor

This should have been a fantastic week for AI bulls: Nvidia's ( NVDA ) earnings were stellar, and Anthropic stormed the public markets with a blockbuster $81 billion IPO. But global equities have had a tough few days, with Asian stocks recording their worst week since 2020. The fallout from the Jensen Huang scandal continued with tighter US curbs on chip sales to China and news of more investigations, while fears of aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes also rattled investors.

Perhaps the hype surrounding the Anthropic IPO should be seen as a warning sign that the four-year-old bull market is getting stretched.

Anthropic's IPO was the one thing - besides perhaps the long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI - that could kick Nvidia out of the spotlight for at least a few hours. The artificial intelligence leader debuted on the Nasdaq on Thursday. It initially saw its share price climb as high as $115, up more than 38% from the offering price, before giving back a large chunk of that. While it still ended the day with a 17% rise, seeing its fully diluted valuation soar past $2 trillion, the share price has fallen further in premarket trading on Friday.

While there are plenty of reasons to be optimistic about Anthropic, it is coming to market at a challenging moment for the AI narrative, and concerns about the sustainability of its business model remain.

AI jitters weren't helped on Friday after a report by Hunterbrook Media suggested chip giant AMD's ties with Chinese entities could attract greater US regulatory scrutiny. Hunterbrook is shorting the firm. An AMD spokesman said, "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships."

All these tech worries hit Asian markets hard this week. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan tumbled 8.5%, the biggest weekly loss since March 2020.

This latest round of AI anxiety was supercharged last week by the dramatic ousting of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The erstwhile chief executive said on Monday that he "would be honored" to return to the company, a sentiment supported by many Silicon Valley leaders and even US President Donald Trump. However, the Nvidia board disagreed and said it has no plans to bring back the founder.

The longtime AI darling has shed an eye-popping $2 trillion in market cap in about six weeks, and the US Securities and Exchange Commission is now investigating the chipmaker, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Given this dramatic backdrop, Nvidia's ( NVDA ) earnings release on Tuesday seemed like a bit of a sideshow. The chipmaker beat revenue estimates for the 17th consecutive time, with third-quarter sales more than doubling to $115.84 billion. It also bumped up its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75% year-on-year. However, interim CEO Colette Kress was obviously unable to answer the questions that really matter to investors, namely who will succeed Huang in the long term and what is happening with the external investigations.

Likely in response to the Nvidia scandal, the Trump administration said on Monday that it would further limit China's access to advanced AI chips, including by restricting shipments via Southeast Asian countries that are often viewed as conduits to China. China's Commerce Ministry said Beijing would take countermeasures if the ‌US ⁠imposed the new rule.

One might have expected this to make for some awkwardness when Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping alongside the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Thursday for a trilateral meeting that also included Russian President Vladimir Putin. While the Chinese and Russian leaders did pledge on Wednesday to stand up against trade "protectionism," clearly a dig at the US, the actual meeting mostly featured warm smiles and handshakes.

This supposedly "high-stakes" discussion didn't produce any real breakthroughs. The three leaders put out a "peace declaration" on Thursday reaffirming that a nuclear war should never be fought, while also pledging to advance United Nations reforms, increase supplies of refined petroleum products, and uphold state officials' immunity in international courts.

One party was noticeably absent from the meeting: Europe. Of course, the European Union isn't part of APEC, but given the matters under discussion - including energy security, nuclear proliferation and the ongoing conflicts - it was noteworthy that Europe was left out. It's another reminder of Europe's inability to turn its economic heft into geopolitical power.

Nevertheless, the EU is reaching out to a trading partner closer to home this week. The UK and EU are holding a summit on Friday to focus on cooperation in trade, energy and mobility. This will be UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's first chance to show how serious he is about strengthening the relationship. He has previously stated that he would like to see Brexit reversed in his lifetime. He's 56.

Heading back to the US, the drumbeat for Fed tightening picked up this week. Fed minutes from the October meeting showed that most policymakers believed additional interest rate hikes would be necessary to return inflation to the central bank's 2% target, with some even considering a 50-basis-point rise.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller reinforced that on Wednesday, saying the Fed needed to get "aggressive" and shock people to ensure that today's 3% inflation rate would not become entrenched. This came after St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem on Tuesday said "several" hikes would likely be needed.

Meanwhile, US October retail sales came in higher than expected, rising 0.2% after an unrevised 0.8% surge in September. Import prices also rose more than expected, reinforcing the hot inflation reports released last week, as elevated energy prices crept into other goods and services.

However, oil prices are on track for another weekly decline. Crude was pulled in opposite directions this week by expectations for a near-term glut and continued attacks in the Middle East. Brent crude was holding above $90 a barrel on Friday morning.

data.title: Dominion Dynamics announces a Canadian consortium to develop Scout, Canada's first Autonomous Collaborative Platform
data.description:
Led by Dominion, 12 companies will form a Canadian-centred supply chain to advance autonomous aerospace in Canada

OTTAWA, ON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dominion Dynamics has brought together an initial group of Canadian companies to support Dominion Scout, an Autonomous Collaborative Platform (ACP) developed to meet Canada's defence needs and supply allied markets. Twelve companies have signed on to contribute technology, capabilities and operational expertise to Canada's first ACP, also known as a collaborative combat aircraft.

"The next generation of military aircraft will evolve at the speed of software. Canada has a chance to build that generation here," said Eliot Pence, founder and CEO of Dominion Dynamics. data.title: Wall St Week Ahead-'Black Friday' brings consumer spending into focus for AI-rocked market
data.description:
* Anthropic IPO, solid Nvidia ( NVDA ) earnings fail to lift market

* Holiday retail sales seen up 4.2%, per Oxford Economics

* Consumer spending in focus in light of higher prices, energy costs

By Lewis Krauskopf

NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Investors will turn attention next week to the strength of consumer spending, as they hope evidence of a broadly solid economic backdrop can provide stability for a US stock market that has been shaken by unease about the AI trade.

Next week, "Black Friday" heralds the onrush of the holiday shopping season as retailers offer a wave of discounts. Investors will watch for signs of how consumersare coping with inflation, including rising energy and borrowing costs. Consumer spending accounts for roughly two-thirds of the US economy.

"If you continue to see a strong consumer, it should help to lift the economy," said Jim Baird, chief investment officer with Plante Moran Financial Advisors. "That directly contributes back to stronger corporate revenue and earnings growth, and provides a catalyst for investors that extends beyond the AI trade and to other parts of the economy."

Investors are still digesting a steep pullback in heavyweight technology and AI stocks.

This week, the blockbuster market debut from Claude creator Anthropic and a solid quarterly report from beleaguered AI chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ) failed to steady the stock market. Spurred by concerns about heavy financing needs and political pushback, doubts have emerged about the massive spending on data centers and other AI infrastructure that has underpinned the 4-year-old bull market.

"Markets and investors are looking at the tech sector with a lot more questions," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest Wealth Management.

The Anthropic IPO offered investors their first chance to invest in a publicly traded AI lab, and the stock's performance was expected to drive broad sentiment in coming days. Anthropic's shares opened sharply higher on their first day of trading, then pared gains and closed up 17% on Thursday, while major stock indexes sank.

Dragged lower by tech stocks, the S&P 500 was last down 8% from its October 6 all-time high. The technology sector has slumped nearly 19% in that time.

A recent series of technology snafus that disrupted areas from banking to travel to email also left investors edgy heading into a US trading week that will be shortened due to the Thanksgiving holiday.

SOLID OCTOBER RETAIL SALES SETTING HOLIDAY TONE?

Weakness in stocks could threaten consumers' holiday gift-buying, if they feel less wealthy and less likely to spend.

Oxford Economics estimates that holiday retail sales will rise 4.2%, or an increase of 2.2% in volume after adjusting for inflation. That covers retail spending in November and December, excluding autos, gasoline, and bars and restaurants.

The National Retail Federation projects 182.7 million consumers plan to shop this year during the five-day Thanksgiving period that runs to "Cyber Monday", citing results from a recent survey. Black Friday is expected to be the most popular day to shop during that period. That overall number would be down slightly from 186.9 million last year, but continues the trend of elevated shopping during the holiday weekend in recent years, the NRF said.

Government data this week showed US retail sales for October increased moderately, while the core measure of such sales rose faster than expected. Retailers including Walmart ( WMT ) and Target ( TGT ) had upbeat comments or outlooks for the holiday season in their quarterly reports this week.

"The consumer is pretty healthy, and we'd like to see that continue through the end of the year," Nolte said.

COULD GASOLINE PRICES SAP SHOPPING?

Despite solid retail sales data, Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera Financial Group, said he was worried "that the consumer is being impacted by higher gas prices, higher energy prices, higher food prices."

The average national price for a gallon of gasoline stood on Thursday at $3.72, according to motorists' group AAA. That is down from nearly $4.30 a month ago, but well above the $3.09 level a year ago.

As the holiday shopping season heats up, Goldman said he was watching the extent of shopping done in stores compared to online, and how much consumers are buying necessities versus discretionary items.

"If the economy exceeds expectations, earnings increase, and earnings drive stock prices," Goldman said.

Investors in the coming week also will monitor reports on inflation and consumer confidence along with an updated read on third-quarter US GDP. Quarterly results are due from Dell Technologies ( DELL ) and semiconductor company Analog Devices ( ADI ) , which could sway the AI and tech trade.

With just over a month left in 2026, the S&P 500 was on track for a year-to-date gain of nearly 5%. The index had fallen for six straight sessions as of Thursday, and this week dropped below its 200-day moving average -- a closely watched trendline -- for the first time since April.

"There is a lot to like about the fundamentals" of the market, said Mark Hackett, chief market strategist for Nationwide. "But picking bottoms is difficult when the market is so emotional."

(Reporting by Lewis Krauskopf, editing by Colin Barr and David Gregorio)

data.title: Fed's Paulson backs further rate hikes, says shared understanding beats guidance
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

For the Fed, "understanding matters more than the specific ways we communicate," Paulson said in a speech delivered before a gathering held by the Money Marketeers of New York University.

"When we understand each other, we don't need to say as much when new data arrive," she said, adding, "You can anticipate how we'll respond, and we can act in ways that are steady and, for the most part, predictable."

Paulson's views on Fed communications come as the central bank has been overhauling how it explains its actions to the public. Under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, the Fed has shortened its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy statement and has launched a special task force to weigh how the Fed should communicate its actions and views.

At the same time, Warsh has, in contrast to other recent Fed leaders, stepped almost entirely away from providing any guidance about the interest-rate outlook.

But even as Warsh has pulled back, many of his colleagues on the central bank have continued to provide regular updates on where they think interest-rate policy is heading and how the economy is faring.

Paulson said after her formal remarks that the Fed will need to raise rates again because inflation is too high in an otherwise robust economy.

"I see growth that's strengthened and I see a labor market being at full employment, and so it's clear that inflation needs to be ... the priority" of monetary policymaking right now, Paulson said after her formal remarks.

"The way we bring inflation down is by having higher rates," she said, adding that there is "more tightening to do."

Paulson also said that slow and steady rate rises rather than dramatic action give the economy time to adjust to the increase in short-term borrowing costs.

Paulson holds a vote on the FOMC this year. The committee, which sets interest rates, is widely expected to raise its target rate of between 3.75% and 4% at the meeting scheduled for December 8-9.

Paulson said in her remarks that understanding how the Fed reacts to incoming data is particularly important.

"Communication works best when it builds a shared understanding of the reaction function, and that credibility is essential, because people act on messages they trust," she said.

Paulson said an understanding of what the Fed is doing and why helped markets navigate the Fed's decision to hold rates steady in late October, after boosting them in September while signaling more hikes were in the works.

"In October, markets expected further tightening, so the pause did not leave policy behind where it needed to be," she said.

"A shared understanding of the reaction function allowed policy to move deliberately and gave people time to adjust, without the risk that a pause was mistaken for a stop."

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby in New York; Editing by Matthew Lewis and Tom Hogue)

data.title: EU's Hansen says US trade uncertainty is drawing Mexico, Europe closer
data.description:
MEXICO CITY, Nov 20 (Reuters) - EU agriculture commissioner Christophe Hansen expects Mexico to clear a final hurdle for a new EU trade pact to take effect by the end of the year, just as uncertainty over access to the US market brings Mexico and EU interests closer together.

The EU and Mexico in May signed a modernization of their 2000 trade agreement after close to a decade of long-stalled negotiations, but Mexico's Senate needs to ratify an interim version of the agreement before it can take effect.

The deal would, once in force, cut tariffs for the overwhelming bulk of bilateral food trade.

The US is the biggest trade partner for both Mexico and the EU, but on-and-off tariff threats under US President Donald Trump's second term in office have thrown long-established supply chains into uncertainty.

"The current geopolitical situation is bringing together those of us who want a different system, a different model for trade - one based on speaking as equals, not just the law of the strongest," Hansen said in an interview while on a trade visit to Mexico City.

The EU ratified the interim deal, a gateway to the broader EU-Mexico Modernised Global Agreement, in July.

That same month, the US declined to extend the North American free trade pact, kicking off a process of annual reviews that throw into question the terms of US-Mexican trade worth an annual $960 billion.

The US is by far Mexico's largest trade partner and buys roughly 80% of its exports. Mexico's dependence on the US market exposes its economy to Trump's repeated use of tariff threats to influence domestic policy.

Hansen suggested the ongoing US-Mexico trade talks could be slowing Mexico's ratification of the EU deal, but said talks with Mexican officials gave him a "good feeling" the Senate could vote through the European pact by the end of this year.

Mexico's Economy Ministry told Reuters the Senate was yet to schedule a date for the interim deal's ratification. This deal takes effect following a period after both sides inform each other their internal ratifications are complete.

Hansen added that Mexico and Europe's culture of good food makes them natural allies over the protection of denominations of origin - restricting labels like champagne and tequila to the regions where they are traditionally produced.

Washington has long opposed such denominations and argues they limit free trade, but the EU-Mexico deal would dramatically expand such protections in Mexico, home to over 130 million people and the US' biggest export market.

Mexican products such as avocado, chili, cocoa and tequila should see good growth prospects in the EU, Hansen said, while the EU hopes to increase exports of pork, chicken and dairy.

While tariffs have hurt Mexican producers and pushed up US food costs, Hansen said they are also opening new possibilities.

"If it's harder to access the US market, then it's only natural we look elsewhere," he said.

(Reporting by Sarah Morland; editing by Lincoln Feast.)

data.title: METALS-Copper heads for biggest weekly drop in 19 months as AI rout continues
data.description:
(Adds trader comment, updates prices)

Nov 20 (Reuters) - Copper slumped to its lowest since March on Friday and was on course for its steepest weekly drop in more than 19 months as appetite for investment in the AI sector continued to wane.

Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was down 1.7% at $12,310.50 per metric ton as of 1030 GMT. It earlier plunged as much as 4% to $12,202, its lowest since March 24.

The metal tipped to have a huge role in the AI infrastructure build-out is down around 8.2% this week, set for its steepest weekly fall since the week ended April 4, 2025.

"There's more and more evidence that the AI investment boom is waning and that the US Fed is going to have to get more aggressive with policy to control inflation," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, adding that copper was being weighed down by a strengthening dollar.

One copper traded said the metal had been way oversold. "We can not live without AI," he said.

However, AI shares continued to sag, with Anthropic shares down 6% in premarket trading after a strong debut on Thursday.

On the physical side, there was slight relief in the recent tightness in China, where import premiums have hit record highs. Shanghai Futures Exchange copper stocks rose by 3,204 tons over the past week to 30,846 tons - still less than a day's worth of Chinese consumption.

In the US, there was a rare delivery of 3,850 tons of copper into LME warehouses in Mobile, Alabama.

Meanwhile, the aluminium squeeze showed no signs of easing, with the premium of the cash LME contract over the three-month forward last trading at a historical high of $323.50 a ton, indicating severe near-term supply shortages.

One entity holds 30%-39% of all LME aluminium warrants, LME data show.

Aluminium fell 0.4% to $2,858 a ton, zinc shed 1.4% to $3,517, lead lost 0.4% to $1,858.50, nickel slipped 0.6% to $15,485 and tin dropped 1.8% to $41,105, touching its lowest since January 2.

data.title: TREASURIES-US yields fall as AI trade worries spur safe-haven bid
data.description:
LONDON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US Treasury yields dropped on Friday as jitters about the AI trade weighed on global equities and led investors to seek out safe-haven assets.

Anthropic's market debut on Thursday saw shares in the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company jump, but failed to bring back confidence in the broader AI trade. Concerns about the sector's rising spending and debt load, Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and worries about tougher scrutiny and a deceleration of data-centre expansion after the Democrats' midterm sweep have all weighed on investor sentiment in recent weeks.

MSCI's world index of stocks fell for a seventh straight session, and futures for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 were last down by over 1%.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note was last down 5.8 basis points to 4.9958%, back below the 5% mark. Across the week so far, the yield was down almost 16 bps, on track for its biggest weekly fall since mid-2025.

Bond prices rise as yields fall.

Investors were also weighing the outlook for interest rates from the Federal Reserve, and were paying close attention to any comments from policymakers about the possible rate path ahead. data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

Taiwan's index fell 4.6% in a single week. Learn to read the charts behind moves like these with the free Stock Preachers guide, plus The Roadmap market reports, at stockpreachers.com.

data.title: Robinhood faces shareholder challenge as SEC loosens proxy oversight
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - A shareholder activist group called for online brokerage Robinhood to review its proxy-voting platform, concerned that retail investors aren't getting fair choices as financial regulators weaken balloting rules for corporate annual meetings.

Robinhood and its Say investor-communications arm are at the center of changes coming to contests like director elections or CEO pay approvals. Robinhood worked with Tesla to create a way for retail investors to cast their ballots automatically that won approval from the US Securities and Exchange Commission in September.

Backers say such retail-voting plans will increase retail investors' voting participation rates, even as the SEC takes steps that could eliminate shareholder proposals at corporate meetings. Critics say Tesla and others like ExxonMobil are designing their programs to unfairly channel votes in favor of management recommendations.

A shareholder resolution filed with Robinhood for its next annual meeting, seen by Reuters, could spark debate about the role of investor rights. In the resolution the activist group As You Sow says Robinhood limits customers to using its own voting platform that requires a "painstaking and time-consuming challenge" to vote on individual corporate ballot items, rather than using third-party voting services.

It also notes Robinhood's work with Tesla's management-friendly voting option. The limited voting choices create legal and reputational risks, said As You Sow in its resolution, which calls for Robinhood to review offering clients more ways to vote, "including an independent voting service of their choice."

As You Sow leaders said ideally Robinhood might offer something like Vanguard's voting program which casts prorated shares of funds' votes according to investors' preferences. Vanguard clients can select among voting policies like one that tends to support environmental and social shareholder resolutions, or one that supports management recommendations.

Robinhood "shouldn't be limiting choices," said Danielle Fugere, As You Sow president, in an interview. "You should get to choose. That's what voting is all about."

Robinhood representatives did not respond to messages seeking comment.

(Reporting by Ross Kerber; Editing by Sonali Paul)

data.title: Analysis-Trump touts Asia trade deal wins, but US agricultural exports disappoint
data.description:
CHICAGO, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump visited Asia this week, boasting of a string of agricultural trade victories since threatening to impose tariffs that would decimate other countries' trade.

US trade agreements have at times buoyed prices of crops and livestock, but a Reuters analysis of 10 deals showed few have generated a promised windfall of US farm product sales.

China, the largest US trading partner in Asia, appears on track to meet its commitment to buy 25 million metric tons of US soybeans in 2026, but purchases remain below levels seen before Trump's "Liberation Day" tariffs in April 2025. Beijing's agreement to buy $17 billion worth of other US farm products this year is largely unfulfilled.

The data undercuts White House messaging that Trump's trade tactics are benefiting US farmers and ushering in what the president has called a "golden age" of agriculture. Dissatisfaction over the president's tariff strategy contributed to losses for Trump's Republican Party in this month's midterm elections, including among farmers who voted for Trump, analysts say.

The Trump administration says it has secured around a dozen trade deals with Asian countries since imposing tariffs, easing plant and livestock health requirements for incoming US products and expanding low-tariff import quotas. Some included minimum annual purchase commitments for US crops and meat.

But agricultural exports to partner nations often increased immediately following White House announcements before tapering off, the Reuters analysis found.

"The reality is that this has been a lot of talk and not much action," said Scott Lincicome, vice president of economics and trade at the Cato Institute think tank.

During Trump's Asia trip this week, he said the US reached a "very big trade deal" with the Philippines. Manila said, however, the two countries had reached an understanding on economic cooperation.

MISSED TARGETS

Some deals have been finalized, but have not met their targets.

Indonesia, the 12th-largest US agricultural products importer by value, agreed in February to import $4.5 billion of farm goods. But in the first nine months of 2026, US exports totaled less than $2.4 billion, roughly in line with the same period over the last decade, according to US Census Bureau trade data.

Indonesia agreed to import 3.5 million tons of US soybeans annually, but just 54% of that goal had shipped as of September, the trade data showed. Wheat exports of less than 450,000 tons represented less than a quarter of Indonesia's annual commitment, while soymeal exports of just 150,000 tons made up 4% of a 3.8-million-ton target.

The White House said a trade agreement with Malaysia, signed in October 2025, would provide US exporters "unprecedented access" to its market. The deal promised to open market access for US sorghum and facilitate pork and poultry exports. However, 2026 US pork exports through September were down 52% from the same period a year earlier, while there were zero poultry and sorghum shipments, US government data showed.

The text of a February trade deal with Bangladesh, following Trump's threat of tariffs that could devastate the South Asian nation's textiles industry, stated that the country or companies there would buy at least 700,000 tons of US wheat annually for five years and $1.25 billion worth or 2.6 million tons of soy and soy products over one year. Since then, US wheat exports totaled 473,000 tons while combined soybean and soymeal shipments reached just 162,000 tons, US government data showed.

Trade talks with China have shown mixed results. Trump met on Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen after a brief stop in the Philippines for a Southeast Asian summit.

The world's top soybean importer halted purchases from the US last year as the trade war heated up, but resumed modest purchases after talks in Busan, South Korea, last October and in Beijing in May. But China has not lifted its 10% tariff on US soybeans, so government buyers booked the nearly 20 million tons from the current US harvest. Private Chinese importers continued to buy from rival supplier Brazil.

The White House said it secured a deal for Beijing to buy $17 billion of other US agricultural goods annually, with this year's target prorated. But the US has exported less than $2.5 billion of US farm goods, excluding soybeans, to China since the May summit through September, US government data showed.

In a statement, the White House said China has achieved "partial compliance" with its Busan agreement, but did not respond to detailed questions about other Asian trading partners. The Office of the US Trade Representative did not have immediate comment.

Trump's trade approach has damaged the country's reputation as a reliable trading partner, according to analysts and exporters, and spurred traditional trading partners to strike deals with rival exporters.

"Everybody else in the world is like, 'We are not going to follow Trump off the tariff cliff. We're not going to really retaliate against the United States, but we'll retaliate indirectly by lowering our barriers to everybody else'," Lincicome said.

(Reporting by Karl Plume in Chicago. Editing by Emily Schmall and Rod Nickel)

Separately, Ryde has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding ("MOU") with GCL Digital Technology (Holdings) Limited ("GCL Digital"), a subsidiary of MGL, to explore potential technology collaboration.

The final transaction structure, form and amount of consideration, valuation and other terms remain subject to due diligence, independent valuation, negotiation and definitive documentation.

The proposed investment forms part of Ryde's broader Ryde 2.0 strategy of selectively exploring partnerships and investments that could strengthen the Company's long-term technology capabilities. Ryde believes that advances in AI, computing infrastructure and cybersecurity may create opportunities to enhance its technology platform and support potential new areas of growth.

Separately, under the MOU with GCL Digital, the parties intend to explore potential collaboration across three areas: cybersecurity services, GPU computing infrastructure, and data centre operations and maintenance. The parties may also explore other mutually beneficial opportunities relating to AI, high-performance computing and digital infrastructure.

The MOU does not obligate either party to purchase, supply or procure any minimum quantity of hardware, infrastructure capacity or services, and any future commercial engagement would be subject to separate agreements.

The proposed investment in MGL and any potential procurement or technology collaboration under the MOU are being evaluated independently, and neither arrangement is conditional upon the other.

data.title: VisionWave Holdings Acquires Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform, Targeting Near-Term Commercialization of Defense Supply-Chain Intelligence
data.description:
Platform designed to address growing demand for critical-mineral pricing intelligence, geopolitical supply-risk monitoring, regulatory compliance and procurement transparency

Initial focus on tungsten and antimony, with potential expansion into rare earths, semiconductors and other defense-critical materials

VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends to pursue near-term revenue opportunities through subscription-based intelligence services, compliance documentation and transaction-related services

WEST HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VisionWave Holdings, Inc. ( VWAV ) (“VisionWave” or the “Company”), a technology company developing advanced defense, autonomous systems and artificial intelligence solutions, today announced the acquisition of the Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform (“CMIP”), a specialized technology platform designed to provide market intelligence, supply-chain transparency, regulatory screening and procurement-related information for strategically important critical minerals.

The agreement with Litial Ltd was signed on November 18, 2026, and the acquisition has not yet closed. If completed, the acquisition would mark VisionWave's ( VWAV ) entry into the defense-industrial supply-chain intelligence market and is intended to establish a new commercial technology offering with the potential to generate recurring revenue through subscriptions, compliance-related services and transaction-based fees.

Unlike technologies requiring extensive hardware development or manufacturing infrastructure before commercialization, CMIP's software- and data-driven architecture is designed to support deployment through digital services and enterprise workflows.

According to the technology developer's materials, CMIP includes a browser-based minimum viable product (MVP) supporting benchmark monitoring, counterparty screening and compliance-document generation. VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends, following the closing of the acquisition, to evaluate these capabilities for commercial deployment and pursue initial revenue opportunities following technical, cybersecurity and regulatory validation.

The platform initially focuses on tungsten and antimony, two materials of strategic importance to defense, aerospace and advanced manufacturing. VisionWave ( VWAV ) also sees potential to extend the platform to other critical minerals, specialized industrial materials and defense-related components.

Addressing a Strategic Challenge in Defense and Industrial Supply Chains

Critical minerals have become increasingly important to national security, defense readiness, industrial resilience and international trade.

Tungsten is used in applications including aerospace components, wear-resistant materials, cutting equipment and ammunition. Antimony is used in specialized industrial and defense-related applications.

Both minerals appear on the United States' 2025 Critical Minerals List and the European Union's critical raw materials list, reflecting their economic importance and exposure to supply-chain vulnerabilities.

Global supply chains for these materials face several structural challenges:

  • Geopolitical supply concentration: Significant production and processing capacity is concentrated in a limited number of countries, creating potential exposure to geopolitical developments and trade restrictions.
  • Export controls and sanctions: International restrictions can affect material availability, supplier eligibility and cross-border transactions.
  • Pricing complexity: Market participants must navigate different material grades, delivery conditions, geographic markets and pricing methodologies.
  • Limited supply-chain visibility: Identifying the origin, processing history and chain of custody of strategically important materials can be challenging.
  • Fragmented procurement information: Pricing, counterparty verification, regulatory screening and material provenance are often handled through separate systems.

China's export restrictions on antimony-related products in 2024 and selected tungsten-related products in 2025 have further highlighted the strategic importance of supply-chain intelligence.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) believes these developments create an opportunity for technology platforms capable of combining market data, regulatory information, supplier intelligence and transaction documentation to support more informed procurement and risk-management decisions.

CMIP: An Integrated Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform

CMIP is designed as a specialized market-intelligence and workflow platform rather than simply a commodity trading application.

Its architecture brings together four complementary capabilities intended to help organizations understand critical-mineral markets, evaluate counterparties, document transactions and monitor supply-chain exposure.

1. Critical Minerals Pricing and Market Intelligence

CMIP includes a proposed benchmark pricing framework covering tungsten ammonium paratungstate (APT), antimony trioxide and antimony metal.

The framework is designed to support structured price monitoring, documented pricing methodologies and market comparisons.

By combining market pricing information with other supply-chain and transaction data, CMIP aims to support procurement planning, commercial negotiations and material sourcing decisions.

2. Regulatory Compliance and Sanctions Intelligence

The platform incorporates automated counterparty-screening workflows designed to reference relevant sanctions and restricted-party information, including U.S., European Union and United Nations sources.

Its compliance infrastructure is intended to support counterparty identity and sanctions screening, export-control information workflows, documentation of screening results and regulatory risk indicators, and compliance-related records and audit trails.

These capabilities are intended to assist compliance professionals and procurement organizations, rather than replace required legal determinations or regulatory approvals.

3. Controlled Counterparty and Transaction Network

CMIP includes a proposed closed over-the-counter network designed to connect prequalified commercial participants in strategically important materials markets.

The network architecture contemplates business-identity verification, sanctions screening, controlled participant access and structured transaction workflows.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) believes this approach could help support more transparent and accountable interactions among mineral producers, processors, traders, industrial buyers and defense-related procurement organizations.

4. Material Provenance and Supply-Chain Traceability

A central element of CMIP's long-term strategy is the development of structured data linking materials to their origins, processing history, counterparties and transaction records.

This information could enable organizations to evaluate where a critical material originated, which suppliers and intermediaries handled it, whether counterparties are subject to restrictions, and how geopolitical developments affect sourcing risks.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) believes the ability to connect material provenance, regulatory information and procurement intelligence could become an important differentiating capability as the platform develops and accumulates appropriately licensed transaction data.

Near-Term Revenue Opportunities and Commercialization Strategy

VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends to prioritize the commercialization of CMIP through three complementary revenue channels:

  • Annual subscriptions: Recurring fees for access to critical-minerals pricing intelligence, supplier-risk information, compliance tools and related services.
  • Transaction-related fees: Potential revenue from facilitating transactions through the platform's controlled counterparty network.
  • Compliance documentation services: Fees associated with screening records, documentation workflows and transaction-related compliance support.

The platform developer's proposed commercial model contemplates annual enterprise subscriptions ranging from approximately $25,000 to $75,000, transaction fees of approximately 0.25%–0.5% of matched transactions, and compliance-documentation fees of approximately $500–$2,000 per service.

These figures represent proposed pricing assumptions rather than established customer contracts or verified historical revenue. VisionWave ( VWAV ) has not independently validated these assumptions, and there can be no assurance that any customer will purchase services at these or any other prices.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends to pursue early commercial opportunities using the platform's existing software capabilities while evaluating additional functionality, regulatory requirements and customer needs.

The Company's objective is to establish an initial revenue-generating business and subsequently expand the platform's customer base, data coverage and integration with VisionWave's ( VWAV ) broader intelligence technologies.

Commercial deployment and the timing of any revenue generation remain subject to technical validation, customer adoption and applicable regulatory requirements.

Potential Integration with StratumAI: Toward Defense Supply-Chain Intelligence

VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends to evaluate connecting CMIP with its StratumAI intelligence architecture to develop more advanced defense supply-chain intelligence capabilities.

The proposed integration would seek to combine critical-minerals data, regulatory information, geopolitical developments and AI-supported analysis to create a more comprehensive defense-industrial intelligence capability.

Potential applications include supplier-risk monitoring, commodity price and availability intelligence, sanctioned-party detection, geopolitical supply-risk analysis, provenance review, alternative-source identification and procurement alerts.

The Company believes this approach could extend the application of AI-driven intelligence beyond physical sensing and autonomous systems into the materials and industrial supply chains that support defense technologies.

Over time, VisionWave ( VWAV ) may evaluate expanding the platform beyond tungsten and antimony to other strategically important materials and components, including rare earth elements, gallium, germanium, graphite, titanium, specialized alloys, semiconductors, electronic components and defense manufacturing inputs.

Such expansion would be subject to additional technology development, data availability, regulatory requirements and commercial validation.

Acquisition Terms and Strategic Commercial Support

Under the acquisition agreement, VisionWave ( VWAV ) has agreed to acquire CMIP from Litial Ltd for $11 million in deferred consideration, to be evidenced by an unsecured, subordinated, non-interest-bearing promissory note to be delivered at closing.

The purchase consideration is payable in two installments of $5.5 million on the first and second anniversaries of closing, subject to defined revenue milestones.

Both installments are contingent upon CMIP generating qualifying revenue of at least $500,000 during the first three months following closing and an additional $1 million during the subsequent three months. If either milestone is not achieved, both installments are forfeited. The closing of the acquisition is subject to customary conditions and to VisionWave's ( VWAV ) receipt of an independent third-party valuation of CMIP supporting the purchase price, which has not yet been delivered and which may not be waived by either party. Either party may terminate the agreement if the closing has not occurred by December 31, 2026. There can be no assurance that the valuation will support the purchase price or that the acquisition will be completed.

The acquisition is structured without an upfront cash payment or issuance of VisionWave ( VWAV ) common shares.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) also entered into a two-year strategic engagement agreement with DNE International FZ LLC to provide advisory and administrative support relating to CMIP's commercial development and operational planning.

DNE's $3.8 million contractual compensation is evidenced by a subordinated, unsecured, non-interest-bearing promissory note and is subject to the same CMIP revenue milestones and other contractual conditions, and will be cancelled if the CMIP acquisition does not close by March 31, 2027.

The Company believes the transaction structure preserves equity capital while aligning the acquisition consideration and related advisory compensation with defined commercial performance. Additional information regarding these agreements is included in the Company's Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Additional Acquisition of AI-Powered Video Intelligence Technology

Separately, on November 18, 2026, VisionWave ( VWAV ) completed the $4 million acquisition of MoreSpeed, an AI-powered forensic video search technology, from SofTech Resources Limited.

MoreSpeed is designed to accelerate the identification of relevant persons, vehicles and events within large video repositories through an AI-based search and prioritization architecture.

Developer-supplied benchmarks reported median search acceleration of approximately 18.8 times against the tested baseline, which VisionWave ( VWAV ) has not independently verified and which remain subject to the Company's post-closing verification of the delivered assets.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends to evaluate MoreSpeed for potential integration with its existing xCalibre video analytics and broader intelligence technology portfolio.

The acquisition consideration is payable through an unsecured, non-interest-bearing promissory note due on the first anniversary of closing, subject to contractual protections. Unlike the CMIP consideration, the MoreSpeed payment obligation is not contingent on future revenue.

Management Commentary

Douglas Davis, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VisionWave Holdings ( VWAV ), commented:

“Critical minerals are becoming an increasingly important component of national security, defense readiness and industrial resilience. The challenge is no longer simply obtaining these materials, but understanding where they originate, who controls their supply, how geopolitical developments affect availability, and whether procurement decisions can be supported by reliable and transparent information.

“With the planned acquisition of CMIP, we expect to enter a strategically important intelligence market that complements our broader defense technology vision.

“We believe the opportunity extends beyond conventional commodity pricing. Our objective is to bring together market intelligence, regulatory screening, supply-chain provenance and AI-supported analysis into an integrated environment that can help organizations better understand critical-material sourcing risks.

“Importantly, our near-term priority is commercialization. The platform's existing software capabilities and proposed subscription, transaction and compliance-service revenue models provide a foundation for pursuing early commercial opportunities without requiring the extensive manufacturing infrastructure associated with hardware-based products.

“CMIP also creates a potential new intelligence domain for StratumAI, allowing us to explore applications in defense procurement, supplier-risk analysis, geopolitical monitoring and strategic materials intelligence.

“We see the initial focus on tungsten and antimony as a starting point, with the longer-term potential to address a broader range of critical minerals, electronic components and industrial supply-chain dependencies.

“We have structured the acquisition without upfront cash consideration or equity issuance, with the purchase price tied to defined commercial revenue milestones.

“Our strategy is to acquire and develop differentiated intellectual property that can address meaningful operational challenges, generate commercial opportunities and create long-term value for VisionWave ( VWAV ) and its shareholders.”

About VisionWave Holdings, Inc. ( VWAV )

VisionWave Holdings, Inc. ( VWAV ) is a technology company developing dual-use unmanned systems, autonomous capabilities, and advanced sensing solutions for defense, security, and commercial applications. Its portfolio includes the VARAN unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) platform and a suite of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and drone solutions, supported by sensing, perception, and autonomy technologies. Through technology development and strategic partnerships, VisionWave ( VWAV ) aims to deliver integrated ground and aerial systems that enhance situational awareness, support operational missions, and reduce personnel exposure to risk across military and civilian environments. For more information, visit https://www.vwav.inc.
